titleEn: When a Walmart closes, what happens to nearby stores?
titleZh: 沃尔玛关店后，附近的商铺会怎样？
method: Machine reference translation with paragraph alignment; not manually certified.

paragraphs.en: Shoppers often greet the closure of a Walmart with dismay, while competitors find cause to celebrate.
paragraphs.zh: 购物者经常沮丧地迎接沃尔玛的关闭，而竞争对手则有理由庆祝。

paragraphs.en: Among critics of the big-box behemoth, a long-held assumption is that once a Walmart disappears, shoppers seeking groceries, household goods, meals and services will flow to businesses down the road.
paragraphs.zh: 在批评沃尔玛的人中，一个长期存在的假设是，一旦沃尔玛消失，寻求杂货、家庭用品、餐饮和服务的购物者将流向未来的企业。

paragraphs.en: But what if the economic downside of a closure is bigger?
paragraphs.zh: 但如果关闭对经济的负面影响更大呢？

paragraphs.en: We are marketing scholars who have studied dozens of Walmart closures in the United States. We found that nearby stores saw a slump in both monthly shopper traffic and sales revenue by roughly a quarter in contrast to comparable stores near Walmart locations that remained open. Our sample covered 39 Walmart stores that closed across 20 states from 2019 to 2026.
paragraphs.zh: 我们是营销学者，研究了美国数十家沃尔玛关闭的门店。我们发现，与沃尔玛附近仍在营业的同类门店相比，附近门店的月客流量和销售收入都下降了约四分之一。我们的样本涵盖了2019年至2026年关闭的39家沃尔玛门店，这些门店遍布20个州。

paragraphs.en: This finding suggests a large retailer can play two roles at once. Walmart competes with neighboring businesses for shopper visits and spending. But it can also act as an anchor, giving people a reason to travel to a shopping area in the first place. When that anchor disappears, the loss of shared shopper traffic can outweigh the benefit of having one less competitor.
paragraphs.zh: 这一发现表明，一家大型零售商可以同时扮演两个角色。沃尔玛与邻近企业竞争顾客到访和消费。但它也可以充当锚，让人们有理由首先前往购物区。当这个锚消失时，共享购物者流量的损失可能超过少一个竞争对手的好处。

paragraphs.en: The benefits of an anchor
paragraphs.zh: 锚的好处

paragraphs.en: Our finding underscores that retailers don’t operate as isolated dots on a map. Shoppers often decide where to go before deciding which stores they’ll visit once they get there. A trip to Walmart can generate a stop at a nearby restaurant, pharmacy, salon, specialty retailer or service business.
paragraphs.zh: 我们的发现强调了零售商并不是地图上孤立的点。购物者通常会先决定去哪里，然后再决定他们到达那里后会去哪些商店。去沃尔玛的旅行可能会在附近的餐馆，药房，沙龙，专业零售商或服务企业停留。

paragraphs.en: Economists call this kind of benefit an agglomeration effect: Businesses can gain from being near other businesses because the location itself attracts shoppers. Shopping center owners have long recognized this logic by using prominent stores to anchor a mix of tenants.
paragraphs.zh: 经济学家称这种好处为聚集效应：企业可以从靠近其他企业的位置中获益，因为位置本身吸引了购物者。购物中心的所有者早就认识到了这一逻辑，他们利用知名商店来锚各种租户。

paragraphs.en:
Other researchers have found that Walmart’s entry into a shopping area causes sales in nearby existing stores to drop.
But these shops can adjust their product assortment, prices and promotions to mitigate this effect, follow-up studies suggest. What has not been studied until now is what happens when a Walmart store – or any other anchor store – closes.
paragraphs.zh:
其他研究人员发现，沃尔玛进入购物区会导致附近现有商店的销售额下降。
但后续研究表明，这些商店可以调整产品种类、价格和促销活动，以减轻这种影响。到目前为止，人们还没有研究过沃尔玛商店--或其他任何锚店--关闭时会发生什么。

paragraphs.en: A Walmart closure creates a tug-of-war between two forces, we argue. Competitive relief helps nearby businesses because a formidable rival is gone. But agglomeration loss hurts them because fewer shoppers have a reason to visit the area.
paragraphs.zh: 我们认为，沃尔玛的关闭会在两股力量之间引发一场拉锯战。竞争力的缓解有助于附近的企业，因为一个强大的竞争对手消失了。但聚集效应的丧失会伤害到它们，因为有理由光顾该地区的购物者减少了。

paragraphs.en: This means a store can capture a larger share of local consumer demand after Walmart leaves and still end up worse off if the total pool of shoppers arriving in the area shrinks enough.
paragraphs.zh: 这意味着，在沃尔玛离开后，一家商店可以抓住当地消费者需求的更大份额，如果到达该地区的购物者总数减少到足够的程度，最终情况仍然会更糟。

paragraphs.en: What happened after a Walmart closed
paragraphs.zh: 沃尔玛关门后发生了什么

paragraphs.en: We combined closure dates with monthly store-level shopper traffic and spending data. For each closed Walmart, we identified nearby non-Walmart businesses and compared their post-closure performance with that of businesses near Walmarts that stayed open.
paragraphs.zh: 我们将关闭日期与每月商店层面的购物者流量和支出数据相结合。对于每个关闭的沃尔玛，我们确定了附近的非沃尔玛企业，并将其关闭后的表现与沃尔玛附近仍然营业的企业进行了比较。

paragraphs.en: We discovered not just a sizable decline in both shopper traffic and sales revenue after closure but a worsening trend in both over time. Specifically, following a Walmart’s closure, nearby stores experienced a roughly 5% drop in the following month and 6% in the month thereafter. The decline keeps getting worse, reaching about 17% in the ninth month and 20% a year after the anchor store closes.
paragraphs.zh: 我们发现，沃尔玛关闭后，不仅客流量和销售收入都大幅下降，而且随着时间的推移，两者都有恶化的趋势。具体来说，沃尔玛关闭后，附近商店在接下来的一个月里下降了约5%，在之后的一个月里下降了6%。这种下降继续恶化，在第九个月达到约17%，在锚店关闭后一年内下降了20%。

paragraphs.en: That parallel movement in traffic and sales matters. If nearby stores were simply selling less to the same number of shoppers, we would expect spending per visit to fall. Instead, what was also happening is that fewer shoppers visited nearby businesses after the anchor disappeared.
paragraphs.zh: 客流量和销售额的平行移动很重要。如果附近的商店只是向相同数量的购物者销售更少的商品，我们会预计每次访问的支出会下降。相反，在锚消失后，光顾附近商店的购物者也会减少。

paragraphs.en: In short, competitive relief didn’t overcome the loss of traffic that would have been generated by trips to the anchor store. But not all nearby businesses were affected equally.
paragraphs.zh: 简而言之，竞争压力的缓解并没有弥补前往锚店的客流量损失，但并非所有附近的商家都受到了同样的影响。

paragraphs.en: Stores that competed more directly with Walmart had better post-closure sales than noncompeting stores. That is what we would expect if competitive relief is real: Grocery stores and other close substitutes are better positioned to capture some of the displaced consumer demand.
paragraphs.zh: 与沃尔玛直接竞争的商店在关闭后的销售额比没有竞争的商店要好，如果竞争缓解是真实的，这就是我们所期望的：杂货店和其他类似的商店更有能力抓住一些被取代的消费者需求。

paragraphs.en: Well-known brand stores also fared relatively better than unbranded businesses. A recognizable brand can give shoppers an independent reason to visit, reducing reliance on traffic generated by the nearby anchor. And stores surrounded by more outlets with its own brands also had more favorable post-closure sales.
paragraphs.zh: 知名品牌商店的表现也相对好于无品牌商店。知名品牌可以给购物者一个独立的理由来光顾，减少对附近锚产生的流量的依赖。而且，被更多自有品牌商店包围的商店在关闭后的销售也更有利。

paragraphs.en: Another important factor is digital reach. Not surprisingly, the more a business engages with customers online, the less it depends on people physically traveling to a cluster of stores. We found that stores with a higher share of revenue from online orders saw a less severe drop in sales after a Walmart closed.
paragraphs.zh: 另一个重要因素是数字覆盖率。毫不奇怪，一家企业在网上与顾客接触越多，它对人们前往一群商店的依赖就越少。我们发现，在线订单收入占比较高的商店，在沃尔玛关门后销售额的下降幅度就不那么大。

paragraphs.en: These patterns suggest that managers have options and can act: Opening another location or expanding online sales can protect a retailer from an anchor closure.
paragraphs.zh: 这些模式表明，管理者有选择，可以采取行动：开设另一个地点或扩大在线销售可以保护零售商免受锚关闭。

paragraphs.en: Why a store closing can become a neighborhood shock
paragraphs.zh: 为什么一家商店的关闭会成为一个邻里震惊

paragraphs.en: A large retailer decides whether to keep a store open based primarily on what makes sense for its own portfolio. But the surrounding businesses face a different calculation. A location that looks weak from the anchor retailer’s perspective can still drive valuable traffic to neighboring stores.
paragraphs.zh: 一家大型零售商决定是否让一家商店继续营业，主要是基于它自己的产品组合是否合理。但周围的企业面临着不同的计算。一个在锚零售商看来薄弱的位置仍然可以为邻近的商店带来有价值的流量。

paragraphs.en: That creates what economists call an externality – a positive or negative effect of an economic activity that impacts other parties even though market prices don’t reflect it. In this case, some of the economic value produced by an anchor sits outside the anchor’s own sales and profits.
paragraphs.zh: 这就产生了经济学家所说的外部性--一种经济活动的正面或负面影响，尽管市场价格并没有反映出来，但它会影响其他各方。在这种情况下，锚产生的部分经济价值不包括在锚自身的销售和利润之外。

paragraphs.en: For neighboring businesses, the lesson is not to assume that a powerful competitor’s departure will create a windfall. Rather, managers need to know how many customers arrive because of the broader shopping destination, not merely how much their store’s products overlap with the anchor’s.
paragraphs.zh: 对于邻近的企业来说，教训是不要想当然地认为一个强大的竞争对手的离开会带来意外之财，相反，管理者需要知道有多少顾客是因为更广泛的购物目的地而到来的，而不仅仅是他们商店的产品与锚的产品有多少重叠。

paragraphs.en: Meanwhile, commercial property owners should treat losing an anchor as more than risking an empty storefront. It can also hurt the rest of their portfolio by reducing consumer demand. Replacing the tenant quickly matters, but so does finding a replacement that can generate trips to the area.
paragraphs.zh: 与此同时，商业地产业主应该把失去一个锚视为比一个空店面的风险更重要的事情。它还可能通过减少消费者需求而损害他们投资组合的其他部分。迅速更换租户很重要，但找到一个可以吸引人们前往该地区的替代者也很重要。

paragraphs.en: Finally, local governments and economic development organizations need to understand that a major retail closure may affect businesses with no contractual relationship to the closed store. So their responses should extend beyond the vacant property itself – whether it’s speeding redevelopment, coordinating with local businesses and property owners to improve shoppers’ access, or helping create a new destination that restores shopper traffic.
paragraphs.zh: 最后，地方政府和经济发展组织需要明白，大型零售店关闭可能会影响到与关闭的商店没有合同关系的企业。因此，他们的应对措施应该超越空置物业本身--无论是加快重建，与当地企业和业主协调以改善购物者的访问，还是帮助创建一个新的目的地以恢复购物者流量。
